Influenza, rhinoviruses, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19 remain active. Children, the elderly, and individuals with chronic conditions are at higher risk. The national campaign 'Respirar é Viver: um Futuro mais Verde' by ABR and ABORL-CCF will stage a Brasília event on June 28, 2026 at Praça do Buriti to promote respiratory health, prevention, and air quality. Distinguishing features: influenza typically causes higher fever, body aches, and fatigue; colds are milder with nasal symptoms. Preventive measures include up-to-date vaccination, regular hand hygiene, avoiding close contact with symptomatic individuals, well-ventilated spaces, and healthy lifestyle; Vitamin C alone does not prevent illness. Seek emergency care for shortness of breath, persistent fever, dehydration, or worsening symptoms in young children, the elderly, or chronically ill individuals.

triage.headline_ja: インフルエンザか風邪か？呼吸器ウイルスの季節を乗り切る方法
triage.triage_reason: 季節性呼吸器ウイルスの一般的な啓発記事であり、新規の異常イベント、集団発生、または深刻な公衆衛生上の危機を示す情報がない。
triage.notes: 本記事は季節性呼吸器ウイルス（インフルエンザ、RSV、COVID-19）について、一般的な予防方法と症状識別に関する公衆衛生啓発コンテンツである。ブラジルで進行中の定型的な季節現象の説明に過ぎず、新規の集団発生、異常な重症度、国際的拡大リスク、または管理不可能性を示す証拠がない。6月28日のイベント予告も予防キャンペーンの一環であり、危機的なシグナルではない。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola - L'OMS constate une accélération de la transmission
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola - WHO notes an acceleration in transmission.
article.articleSummary: Ebola transmission in the Democratic Republic of Congo accelerates despite reinforced response measures. As of 19 June 2026, 75 healthcare workers have been infected and 17 of them have died. Transmission is rapidly expanding across 33 health zones in three provinces. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is no vaccine or specific treatment. The DRC declared its 17th Ebola epidemic on 15 May. WHO Africa emergencies director Marie Roseline Belizaire stated that the situation remains grave and evolving, even as the response strengthens daily. No details are provided on laboratory confirmation or infection sources beyond frontline transmission, and there is no mention of imported or exported cases. The report highlights urgent needs for infection prevention and control among health workers amid ongoing spread.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ - WHOが感染拡大の加速を指摘
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準において深刻な公衆衛生上の影響、異常/予想外な事象、国際的拡大リスクの3基準に該当。WPROスクリーニング基準でも重症度（死亡者17名、医療従事者感染）、流行可能性（複数省の33保健圏での急速拡大）、管理可能性（ワクチンなし、国際支援必要）に該当。
triage.notes: コンゴ民主共和国における第17次エボラ流行。Bundibugyo株（ワクチン・特異的治療なし）による急速な伝播。医療従事者への感染が著しく、3州33保健圏での拡大が確認されている。WHOアフリカ地域事務局による高い関心が示されている。国際的な支援・注視が必須のシグナル。

article.articleHeadline: Epidemia de ebola se propaga rapidamente na RD Congo, alerta OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola epidemic spreads rapidly in the DRC, WHO warns.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is spreading rapidly, according to the World Health Organization. Ituri province accounts for more than 90% of known cases, with transmission also reported in North Kivu and South Kivu. The outbreak was declared on May 15 and involves the rare Bundibugyo strain. As of the latest WHO report, 896 cases and 232 deaths have been confirmed, with 21 new cases in the last 24 hours. Health teams have expanded capacity, with treatment beds rising from zero to more than 500; surveillance now handles about 400 alerts daily and conducts over 2,000 tests per day. Contact tracing covers roughly 75% of identified contacts, with a target of 95% to control the outbreak. Ebola spreads through close contact with infected bodily fluids; improved detection enables safer, dignified burials and reduces risk to families. Ongoing conflict in Ituri complicates the response.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行がコンゴ民主共和国で急速に拡大、WHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラウイルス病の急速な流行拡大、複数州への広がり、国際的拡大リスク、および渡航・貿易制限の可能性がある。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo株によるエボラ流行で、896例の確定患者と232死亡が報告されている。複数州（Ituri、North Kivu、South Kivu）への拡大、Ituri州での紛争が対応を複雑にしている。接触者追跡率75%だが目標95%という管理課題あり。WHOが公式警告を発出している。フルRRA実施が推奨される。

article.articleHeadline: La epidemia de ébola se propaga rápidamente en la RDC, advierte la OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic is spreading rapidly in the DRC, WHO warns.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is spreading rapidly, per the World Health Organization. The latest counts report 896 laboratory-confirmed cases and 232 deaths, with 21 new infections in the last 24 hours. The outbreak is centered in Ituri province (over 90% of cases) and has extended to North Kivu and South Kivu. The Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain is involved; transmission was undetected for a period after the outbreak was declared on May 15. Response capacity has improved, including over 500 Ebola treatment beds (up from zero), about 400 alerts daily, and more than 2,000 tests per day. Contact tracing covers about 75% of contacts; the goal is 95% for control. Transmission occurs via close contact with infected fluids; safe, dignified burials reduce risk. In Uganda, 19 cases, 2 deaths, 10 recoveries; no new cases in 12 days.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行がDRCで急速に拡大、WHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当し、WPROスクリーニング基準5つすべても該当。エボラウイルス病は国際的に重大な懸念事項であり、急速な拡大傾向、複数州への波及、ウガンダへの越境確認により、フルリスク評価が必須。
triage.notes: Bundibugyo ebolavirus株によるDRC内での急速な流行。Ituri州を中心に896件の確定症例、232死亡。ウガンダでも越境感染19症例確認。接触者追跡カバー率75%と不十分。WHOによる警告あり。国際的な支援体制が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola outbreak kills 17 healthcare workers as Chinese medical team arrives in DRC
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has killed 232 people and infected 896, with 75 healthcare workers infected and 17 among them dead. The outbreak, confirmed mid-May after earlier suspicions, is driven by the Bundibugyo virus, for which there are no approved vaccines or treatments. Ituri province is an epicentre, where hygiene infrastructure has nearly collapsed: only about 20% of health centers have access to enough clean water. WHO Emergency Director Marie Roseline Belizaire highlighted the strain on a health system already short on workers (11 per 10,000 people). A Chinese medical team has arrived to assist; Uganda is sending a team as well. The Africa CDC said cases rose 38% in one week, and the outbreak is three times worse at this stage than Uganda’s 2000 outbreak (281 cases). Responses include WHO’s six-month £386m plan and Oxfam’s $11.6m intervention to deliver clean water and hygiene kits.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱の流行で医療従事者17人が死亡、中国医療チームがコンゴ民主共和国に到着
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つ全て該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響：232人死亡、896人感染；異常かつ予想外；国際的拡大リスク：ウガンダ対応、中国チーム派遣；渡航・貿易制限リスク高い）。WPROスクリーニング基準も5つ全て該当。エボラアウトブレイクは最高レベルの懸念事項。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはコンゴ民主共和国（DRC）のイツリ州でのエボラ流行が主題。ウガンダはDRCの対応を支援する側として言及されており、発生地ではない。中国チームの到着は支援活動であり、中国での発生ではない。Bundibugyo virus (BDBV)による流行、高い致命率、医療従事者の高い感染率（75名中17名死亡）が報告されており、公衆衛生危機として最高レベル。

article.articleHeadline: Не посустаје епидемија еболе у Демократској Републици Конго: Више од 230 мртвих, скоро 900 заражених
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo continues unabated: more than 230 dead, nearly 900 infected.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-06-19, the Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo persists, with 232 deaths and 896 confirmed infections. In the last 24 hours, six deaths and 21 new cases were recorded. The outbreak began on 15 May in eastern DRC, with transmission also reported in neighboring Uganda. The World Health Organization describes Ebola as a severe, often fatal disease, with an average case fatality around 50%. Early symptoms include sudden fever, marked weakness, muscle pains, headache, and sore throat, followed by vomiting, diarrhea, rash, kidney and liver dysfunction, and, in some cases, internal or external bleeding. Transmission occurs through direct contact with blood, bodily fluids, or tissues of infected humans or animals; infected persons are infectious as long as the virus is in their blood and secretions. Health workers and close contacts are at highest risk.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行が継続：230人以上の死亡、約900人の感染者
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目すべてが該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際拡大リスク、渡航・貿易制限リスク）。エボラ出血熱の進行中の流行で、致死率約50%、複数国での確認。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーではDRCとウガンダでの伝播が言及されているが、ウガンダ（1562822）は対象国リストに含まれていないため、verified_locationsではDRCのみを列挙。進行中の流行で232人の死亡、896人の確認感染者。WHO認定の高リスク疾患。

article.articleHeadline: WHO: 75 Pflegekräfte mit Ebola infiziert
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: 75 healthcare workers infected with Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Two Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda have resulted in 896 confirmed infections and 232 deaths, including 75 healthcare workers infected and 17 of them dead. WHO spokesperson Marie-Roseline Belizaire in Bunia said infections are not always clearly linked to workplace exposure. The WHO is delivering gloves and protective clothing to small clinics and training staff to reduce transmission. Of 177 clinics surveyed, only four had the capacity and materials to adequately protect all staff. A major challenge is that only about 10% of Ebola cases present with bleeding, leading many patients to stay home believing they have malaria and delaying admission to Ebola treatment centers, increasing household and small-clinic spread. As of June 19, 2026, the outbreak remains serious and evolving.

triage.headline_ja: WHO：75人の医療従事者がエボラに感染
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当し、複数国に広がるエボラウイルス病アウトブレイク。医療従事者を含む高い死亡率と国際的懸念が存在。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーは「Democratic Republic of CongoとUgandaでのエボラアウトブレイク」と述べているが、提供対象国リストではDRC（ID:203312）のみが該当する。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため除外。896確認感染、232死亡、医療従事者75名感染・17名死亡という深刻な状況。感染拡大の主要因は医療施設の防護装備不足とマラリアとの鑑別困難性が指摘されている。WHOが積極的に対応中。

article.articleHeadline: El hambre se convierte en un obstáculo clave para contener el ébola en Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Hunger becomes a key obstacle to containing Ebola in Congo
article.articleSummary: Food insecurity in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo is undermining Ebola containment as hunger drives patients to flee treatment and isolation centers. In Bambu, near Mongbwalu, 11 suspected Ebola patients escaped a hospital due to insufficient food, highlighting nutrition gaps amid the outbreak. Since late May, government reports document more than 150 breaches of Ebola treatment and isolation centers; the outbreak has infected nearly 900 people and killed more than a quarter. About 6,400 individuals are under monitoring for potential exposure, while roughly 10 million residents face acute food insecurity in the eastern provinces, hampering surveillance and containment. Ituri province accounts for over 90% of confirmed cases. The World Food Programme stresses that without food aid, confinement is ineffective, with grave implications for households headed by single mothers, minors, or the elderly.

triage.headline_ja: 飢饉がコンゴのエボラ封じ込めの大きな障害となる
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常な状況、国際的拡大リスク）。エボラ出血熱の大規模流行で既に900人感染、死亡者多数。食糧不足により患者が隔離施設から逃亡し、150件以上の違反と600万人以上が監視対象という深刻な状況。
triage.notes: Bluedot APIが検出した発生地域にイタリア（Veneto州、Bambù）が含まれているが、記事サマリーではイタリアでの発生は記載されていない。Bambùはコンゴ東部の地名として登場し、イタリアではなくコンゴ内の地域。したがって verified_locations はDRCのみ。エボラウイルス病の大規模流行であり、食糧不足による隔離施設からの患者逃亡と監視対象者の増加は、コンテインメント失敗と国際的拡大のリスクを示唆。早急なフルRRA実施が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 75 медици са били заразени с ебола от началото на епидемията в Конго през май
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 75 healthcare workers have been infected with Ebola since the start of the Congo epidemic in May.
article.articleSummary: Seventy-five healthcare workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak began in May, with 17 deaths, according to the World Health Organization. Transmission is believed to have occurred for months before Congolese authorities declared the outbreak on May 15, exposing many health workers unaware of the disease. Health facilities report dwindling supplies of basic PPE, such as gloves and masks. Five people have recovered from the new Ebola strain. WHO Emergencies Director Marie Rozlin Belizer described the toll on the health system, noting the DRC’s very low health workforce (about 11 per 10,000 people). The situation underscores ongoing risk to frontline workers and the need for sustained PPE, staffing, and support in eastern DRC.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでのエボラ流行開始以来、75人の医療従事者が感染（5月から）
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準2つ以上該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、国際的拡大リスク）。また、WPROスクリーニング基準でも異常性、重症度、流行しやすさが確認され、社会的関心が高い。フルRRAに進む必要あり。
triage.notes: DRCでのエボラ流行は2026年5月15日に当局により正式宣言。医療従事者への感染が集中（75人中17人死亡）。PPE不足が深刻で、DRCの医療従事者不足（10,000人あたり約11人）は対応能力に重大な懸念を示している。WHOが既に関与し、国際支援の必要性が明確に認識されている。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola spreading 'fast' in DR Congo, warns WHO
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is spreading rapidly, driven by the Bundibugyo strain for which there is no vaccine. Declared May 15, the outbreak has 896 confirmed cases and 232 deaths, with 21 new cases reported in the last 24 hours. Over 90% of known cases are in Ituri province, though transmission has expanded to North Kivu and South Kivu. WHO Africa emergencies chief Marie-Roseline Belizaire, speaking from Bunia, said the situation is serious and evolving quickly, yet response capacity is expanding: beds for Ebola patients have risen from zero to over 500; surveillance teams are investigating nearly 400 alerts and can conduct more than 2,000 tests per day. About 75% of contacts are being traced, with a 95% target. Transmission occurs via close contact and infected bodily fluids. In neighboring Uganda, 19 cases (2 deaths, 10 recovered) have been reported, with no new cases in 12 days.

triage.headline_ja: エボラがコンゴ民主共和国で「急速に」拡大している、とWHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当し、かつWPRO基準5項目全て該当。エボラ出血熱の国際的感染症で、複数国（DRC・ウガンダ）に拡大しており、死亡率も高く公衆衛生上の重大な脅威である。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでウガンダの事例言及があるも、発生地域（location_type=6）として対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。ウガンダはスクリーニング対象国に含まれていないため除外。エボラ出血熱（Case Fatality Rate 約25.9%）による896確認症例232死亡は極めて深刻。ワクチン未対応の株（Bundibugyo strain）による急速な拡大が最大の懸念。

article.articleHeadline: KDC'de Ebola salgınında durum ciddiyetini sürdürüyor" - Havadis Gazetesi | Kıbrıs Haber
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: In KDC, the Ebola outbreak situation remains serious.
article.articleSummary: In the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Ebola outbreak remains serious one month after declaration. Ituri province reported the initial signals (246 suspected cases and 65 deaths) with the outbreak declared on May 15 and the WHO declaring an international public health emergency on May 17. As of June 19, 2026, the outbreak has spread across 3 provinces and 33 health zones, totaling 896 laboratory-confirmed cases and 232 deaths. Uganda has not reported cases in the last 12 days. The World Health Organization states response efforts must be intensified, with over 115 WHO staff deployed to affected areas. Operational needs rise as the outbreak widens, and access restrictions in high-risk regions hamper activities. The causative virus is Bundibugyo, a rare Ebola variant for which no approved treatment or vaccine exists.

triage.headline_ja: KDCでエボラ出血熱流行の状況が深刻性を継続している
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つ全て該当。エボラ出血熱は極めて重篤で致死率が高く、複数県での拡大と232名の死亡が報告されている。Bundibugyo株で治療法やワクチンがない点が特に懸念。国際対応が急務。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCでのエボラ出血熱流行を主題としており、Ituri州での初期検出、3州33ヘルスゾーンへの拡大、896件の確定症例、232名の死亡が報告されている。Bundibugyo株は治療法・ワクチンが未承認。ウガンダは12日間新規症例なしとのことだが、接触国としてのリスク監視が必要。WHOが国際保健上の緊急事態を宣言しており、対応スタッフ115名以上が派遣されている。アクセス制限が活動を妨げている点も懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: UE/Cimeira: Líderes europeus preocupados com propagação do Ébola na RDCongo e Uganda
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: EU Summit: European leaders concerned about the spread of Ebola in DR Congo and Uganda.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 June 2026, the European Council warns of ongoing Ebola transmission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Uganda. DRC reports 202 deaths among nearly 900 confirmed cases; Uganda reports 19 cases and 2 deaths. The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo ebolavirus, with a case-fatality rate estimated at 30–50%; there is no licensed vaccine or specific treatment. Transmission occurs via direct contact with bodily fluids of infected people or animals, causing fever, hemorrhagic fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and internal bleeding. The EU commends rapid emergency funding from the WHO and partners, enabling surveillance, contact tracing, clinical preparedness, and expanded laboratory capacity, with financial and logistical support to WHO, Africa CDC, and frontline responders. Leaders urge ongoing monitoring and coordinated priorities, linking the outbreak to broader global health governance challenges and reinforcing WHO-led prevention and response. Sub-Saharan Africa faces elevated risk; global risk remains low.

triage.headline_ja: EU首脳会議：エボラ出血熱のコンゴ民主共和国とウガンダでの拡大に欧州首脳が懸念
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当し、エボラ出血熱の確認事例と死亡者が報告されている。国際的な懸念と対応が進行中であり、フルRRA実施が必要。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーではウガンダ（対象国外）での発生も言及されているが、verified_locationsには対象国であるDRCのみを含める。エボラ出血熱（Bundibugyo ebolavirus）による確認事例902件、死亡221件が報告されており、致命率30-50%、ワクチンや特異的治療法なし。EU首脳会議での協議対象となっており、国際的な懸念度が極めて高い。

article.articleHeadline: WHO: 75 Pflegekräfte mit Ebola infiziert - Deutsches Ärzteblatt
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: 75 nurses infected with Ebola - Deutsches Ärzteblatt
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda: 896 confirmed infections with 232 deaths; 75 health-care workers infected, including 17 nurses. WHO spokesperson Marie-Roseline Belizaire in Bunia reported the figures in Geneva. It is unclear whether infections occurred at work or in private settings. WHO is supplying gloves, protective clothing, and staff training to clinics, but only four of 177 inspected facilities had the capacity and materials to adequately protect workers. A key challenge is that only about 10% of Ebola cases show typical symptoms, particularly bleeding, causing many people to stay home and mistake symptoms for malaria, delaying admission to specialized Ebola treatment centers and increasing transmission within families and small clinics. One month after outbreak declaration, the situation remains serious and evolving.

triage.headline_ja: WHO：75人の看護師がエボラに感染 - ドイツ医師会誌
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当。DRC・ウガンダでのエボラアウトブレイク、232死亡、ヒトヘルスケアワーカーの高い感染率、国際的懸念と対応（WHO関与）が確認されている。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはDRCおよびウガンダでのエボラアウトブレイクを述べているが、対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ。ウガンダは対象国外。ジュネーブはWHO本部の報告地点であり、実際の発生地ではない。エボラの致死性と医療従事者感染の高率は国際的な公衆衛生上の重大リスクを示唆。

article.articleHeadline: "Ți se rupe sufletul". Peste 70 de medici au fost infectaţi cu Ebola de la debutul epidemiei, iar 17 dintre ei au murit
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: "Your heart breaks." More than 70 doctors have been infected with Ebola since the outbreak began, and 17 of them have died.
article.articleSummary: As of June 19, 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo continues to devastate the health system, with 75 doctors infected and 17 dead since the outbreak began. Transmission is believed to have occurred for months before the official declaration on May 15, underscoring delays in recognizing spread. Shortages of basic protective equipment, including gloves and masks, exacerbate care delivery. DRC records one of the lowest health worker densities globally, about 11 doctors per 10,000 people. Uganda and China are dispatching medical teams to assist, while WHO provides psychological support to physicians confronting frequent patient mortality and colleague infections. The report underscores the heavy toll on clinicians and ongoing challenges in protecting frontline staff as authorities work to contain Ebola.

triage.headline_ja: 「心が張り裂ける思いだ」流行開始以来、75人の医師がエボラに感染し、うち17人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目全て該当（公衆衛生への深刻な影響、予想外の医療従事者感染、国際支援の必要性、複数国への拡大リスク）。WPROスクリーニング基準も複数該当。エボラ出血熱は高い死亡率を持つNFL級疾患であり、国際的な関心も高い。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーにおいて、DRCでのエボラ流行が主題であり、UgandaおよびChinaが医療チームの派遣により積極的に関与している。Ugandaは対象国リストに含まれていないため verified_locations に含めない。医療従事者への感染（75人、死亡17人）という異常な規模と医療システムへの深刻な影響が明記されており、国際支援（WHO、中国）も並行している点で複数のリスク基準を満たす。

article.articleHeadline: Maimuțele amazoniene contractează hepatita B umană, iar defrișările agravează situația
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Amazonian monkeys contract human hepatitis B, and deforestation worsens the situation.
article.articleSummary: Human hepatitis B virus (HBV) detected in wild Amazonian monkeys for the first time. In a study by the University of Salford, Federal University of Amazonas, and colleagues, HBV was found in 17 of 49 wild primates living in regions with strong human influence (Rondônia and Mato Grosso in Brazil) but in none of 39 animals from a more isolated stretch along the Japurá River in Amazonas. The findings suggest human population density drives cross-species transmission. Researchers caution deforestation and expanding human settlements raise contact and spillover risk. It remains unclear whether HBV causes disease in these New World monkeys or whether inter-primate transmission occurs. HBV is transmitted via blood or bodily fluids; path from humans to primates is under investigation. Local hunting and wildlife trade intensify contact. The study, published in EcoHealth, underscores zoonotic/anthroponotic risk at human–primate interfaces.

triage.headline_ja: アマゾンのサルが人間のB型肝炎に感染、森林破壊が状況を悪化させている
triage.triage_reason: B型肝炎ウイルスの野生霊長類への逆人獣感染が報告された新知見であり、人獣感染インターフェースでの人獣共通感染症リスクが指摘されている。ただし、現時点では野生動物への検出のみであり、人間への公衆衛生的影響は明確でなく、詳細な疫学情報が不足している。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはブラジル（ロンドニア州およびアマゾナス州）での野生霊長類からのB型肝炎ウイルス検出を報告している。公表されている研究成果であり、直近の人間への健康被害は報告されていないが、森林破壊による人間-野生動物接触増加に伴う人獣共通感染症リスク（逆人獣感染を含む）が懸念される。WPROスクリーニング基準では異常性、長期曝露リスク、流行可能性が該当するが、IHR基準での該当は異常性のみであり、かつ社会政治的関心の情報が不足している。継続的な監視が推奨される。

article.articleHeadline: Zeci de medici s-au îmbolnăvit de Ebola după ce au contractat virusul Bundibugyo în timpul focarului din Congo - HotNews.ro
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dozens of doctors fell ill with Ebola after contracting the Bundibugyo virus during the Congo outbreak.
article.articleSummary: As of June 19, 2026, the Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has 894 laboratory-confirmed cases and over 200 deaths in its first month, with the outbreak spreading to Uganda. The outbreak is believed to have begun months prior to an official May 15 declaration. Seventy-five healthcare workers have been infected, 17 of them dead, highlighting extensive exposure before recognition. The DRC’s health workforce density is low (~11 health workers per 10,000 people), and PPE supplies are running short; Uganda and China are sending medical teams. More than 30,000 people are believed exposed. Bundibugyo virus is rare, with no approved vaccines or treatments and limited early testing. By comparison, Zaire ebolavirus, more common in Congo, has vaccines and has caused most prior outbreaks (16). The virus has crossed borders, with Uganda affected.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴの流行中にブンディブギョウイボラウイルスに感染した医師たちがイボラで倒れた
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべて該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的拡大、渡航・貿易制限リスク）。WPROスクリーニング基準も全5つ該当。極めて高いリスク評価。
triage.notes: 発生地域にUgandaとChinaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではDRCでの流行が主題。Ugandaへの拡大は既述されているが詳細が限定的であり、verified_locationsではDRCのみとした。Chinaについては対象国リストには含まれるが、サマリーでは医療チーム派遣の文脈のみで、イベント発生国ではないため除外。稀なブンディブギョウウイルス、ワクチン・治療法なし、医療従事者の多数感染（17名死亡）、3万人以上の曝露という極めて深刻な状況。

article.articleHeadline: Santé. Ebola en RDC : l'OMS alerte sur une accélération de l'épidémie
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Health. Ebola in the DRC: WHO warns of an acceleration of the outbreak.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 June 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is accelerating, despite reinforced public health responses. The World Health Organization reports rapid evolution of transmission with acceleration in 33 health zones across three provinces. Marie Roseline Belizaire, WHO Africa emergencies director, spoke from Bunia, noting the situation remains grave and continues to evolve, even as response activities are strengthened day by day. With 33 health zones affected across three provinces, the outbreak's spread is widening, complicating containment. The report underscores ongoing transmission and the need for sustained surveillance and intervention across the affected regions.

triage.headline_ja: 健康：エボラ出血熱がコンゴ民主共和国で流行加速、WHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当し、エボラ出血熱の加速する流行は国際的脅威となる。WHOの公式警告があり、複数州33の保健区域に拡大している緊急事態。
triage.notes: エボラ出血熱は高致死率病原体であり、WPROスクリーニング基準5項目すべてに該当。複数州にわたる拡大とWHOの公式警告により、国際的な健康上の危機と判定。対象国DRCで発生確認。

article.articleHeadline: Русија је прва у свету развила ефикасан тест-систем за дијагностику еболе
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Russia was the first in the world to develop an effective test system for diagnosing Ebola.
article.articleSummary: Russia’s Rospotrebnadzor announces the world’s first highly accurate real-time RT-PCR diagnostic system for Ebola, already deployed in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. Moscow claims 100% sensitivity and specificity, with the capability to detect Ebola even in external samples, and notes the virus has mutated to a more infectious Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain. While no Ebola vaccine exists, early detection is deemed critical to outbreak containment. Some Japanese scientists had warned of cross-continental spread, with risk regions including Belgium, France, the United Arab Emirates, Turkey, India, and Canada. Dr. Djedon Mvamba Kazadi urges expanding treatment-center capacity as cases rise. Production aims to cover African needs, with about 7,000 test systems delivered and interest from parts of Asia. International bodies warn of a dangerous trajectory: the CDC notes a risky path, while the UN and EU allocate funds for Central Africa and the Great Lakes region.

triage.headline_ja: ロシアがエボラ診断の効果的なテストシステムを世界で初めて開発
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルスの国際的拡大リスク（複数国への言及）、重症度の高さ、および異常/予想外の病原体変異（Bundibugyo ebolavirus）が確認されており、IHR基準3項目以上、WPROスクリーニング基準複数項目該当。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーではエボラウイルスの国際的拡大の警告、病原体変異（Bundibugyo ebolavirus）への言及、複数国の危険地域としての記載がある。DRC、ウガンダでの配置実績、インドを含むアジア地域での関心が明記されている。対象国リストに含まれる検証可能な発生地は DRC、Uganda、India。その他言及国（ベルギー、フランス、トルコ、UAE、カナダ）は対象国に含まれないため除外。

article.articleHeadline: WHO Health Emergencies EPI-WIN webinar: Safe, scalable Ebola (Bundibugyo) care in DR Congo: operations, clinical guidelines and treatment-centre design
article.articleSummary: DR Congo is contending its 17th Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu. Bundibugyo virus disease has no licensed vaccine or specific treatment; early detection, high-quality supportive care and safe, well-designed treatment facilities are the most effective lifesaving tools. The WHO-hosted EPI-WIN webinar on 24 June 2026, 13:00–14:00 CEST, brings WHO and national experts to review the current operational picture, present newly released comprehensive clinical management guidelines for filovirus disease, and demonstrate humane, scalable treatment-centre designs drawing on Ebola and Marburg standards. Emphasis on early standardized supportive care as the key determinant of survival in the absence of a Bundibugyo-specific therapy. The session features panelists from ALIMA, WHO Congo Office, and WHO Headquarters, and aims to translate global guidance into field delivery for outbreak response.

triage.headline_ja: WHO保健緊急事態EPI-WINウェビナー：コンゴ民主共和国におけるエボラ（ブンディブギョ）安全でスケーラブルなケア：運用、臨床ガイドライン、治療センター設計
triage.triage_reason: DRC内でBundibugyo Ebola outbreakが進行中（17th outbreak）。IHR基準で公衆衛生への深刻な影響（Yes）、異常性（Yes）、国際的拡大リスク（Yes）の3基準該当、WPRO基準でも重症度・流行性・長期曝露でYes。
triage.notes: 記事はBundibugyo Ebola outbreakの現状と対応に関するWHOウェビナー告知だが、DRCで継続中のエボラ流行（Ituri、North Kivu、South Kivu州）を明記。ワクチンなし、治療法なしという点で極めて高リスク。本イベント情報自体は学習・ガイダンス共有だが、背景となる流行は重大かつ複合ウイルス感染（EbolaとMarburg言及）のリスクを含む。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola, leader Ue: preoccupazione per la diffusione della malattia
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola, EU leader: concern over the spread of the disease.
article.articleSummary: June 19, 2026: The European Council expresses concern over the spread of Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda. The conclusions, approved at the leaders’ summit following a request by Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, underscore EU attention to the outbreak. Leaders welcome rapid emergency funding from the World Health Organization and other international and European partners, enabling an immediate response that includes epidemiological surveillance, contact tracing, clinical preparedness, and expanded laboratory capacity. The European Union has activated financial and logistical support to bolster the work of the WHO, Africa CDC, and other humanitarian and health actors coordinating urgent containment and response measures on the ground. No specific case counts or timelines are provided in the brief.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ出血熱、EUリーダー：疾病拡大への懸念
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス病はIHR基準4つすべてに該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、国際的懸念、国間での拡大リスク、渡航制限の可能性）。DRCとウガンダでの同時多発はWPRO基準も満たし、EU・WHOなどの国際的対応が既に開始されており、フルRRA実施が必須。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはDRCおよびウガンダでのエボラ感染症の拡大を述べているが、対象国リストではDRCのみ該当。ウガンダは対象国外のため除外。イタリア言及は記事が配信源（イタリアのニュース媒体）および首相の提言元の背景であり、実際の発生地ではないため除外。EU全体による国際支援の発動と、WHO及びアフリカCDCの関与が明記されており、この状況は明らかなシグナルイベント。

article.articleHeadline: Franklin Graham says Ebola outbreak 'much worse than initially thought;' calls for prayers
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) intensifies, with the northeastern region described as the outbreak epicenter. Samaritan's Purse has opened two 40-bed Ebola treatment centers in Bunia and Nyankunde, supported by about 70 disaster-response staff. No official case or death counts are provided. Government-controlled testing can take four to eight days, hindering rapid confirmation; local labs are lacking. Early symptoms can resemble malaria, prompting an isolation approach for all patients. IV fluids are the main current treatment; antibodies for Ebola are hoped to be available soon. Logistical hurdles include unreliable power, requiring generators, water purification, and independent storage; PPE must be complete and workers limited to roughly 30-minute shifts. Borders are closed between DRC and Uganda; returning personnel to the United States could face quarantine. Publication date: 2026-06-19

triage.headline_ja: フランクリン・グラハム氏がエボラ流行は「最初の予想より遥かに悪い」と述べ、祈りを呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当（重度な公衆衛生影響、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限の実施）。対象国DRCにおけるエボラアウトブレイクの深刻化を示す明確なシグナル。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCのエボラアウトブレイクが主題。Bunia（DRC北東部）が震源地として特定される。マラリアとの鑑別診断の困難さも言及。米国への帰国者の隔離可能性が言及されるが、米国での発生は示唆されておらず、verified_locationsはDRCのみ。ウガンダとの国境閉鎖が記載されるが、ウガンダでのアウトブレイク発生の具体的記述なし。

article.articleHeadline: El Nino Picu Risiko Penyebaran DBD Lebih Luas, IDAI Ingatkan Masyarakat Waspada
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: El Niño Triggers Wider Dengue Transmission Risk, IDAI Warns the Public to Stay Vigilant
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-06-19, El Niño-linked warming and drier conditions raise dengue transmission risk in Indonesia, warn IDAI. In Jakarta, Prof. Hartono Gunardi notes higher sea surface temperatures drive broader warming, boosting Aedes aegypti development and dengue spread. As temperatures rise beyond about 28°C, mosquito biting frequency increases from every five days to roughly every two days, elevating human-to-human transmission risk. Dry spells compel households to store water, creating ideal breeding sites for mosquitoes. Indonesia, a long-standing dengue-endemic country, faces expanded geographic risk as climate change enlarges suitable habitats. Preventive measures urged: regular drainage and covering of water containers, proper disposal of waste that could hold water, and environmental sanitation. Beyond vector control and behavior change, dengue vaccination is highlighted as key to reducing outbreaks amid mounting climate threats.

triage.headline_ja: エルニーニョがデング熱の拡大感染リスクを引き起こす、IDI（インドネシア小児科医学会）が国民に警戒を呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: デング熱はインドネシアの風土病であり、季節的な変動は予想される。現在のところ、具体的な患者数増加や死亡事例の報告がなく、警告段階の予測的な記事である。情報充実後の判定のため要経過観察。
triage.notes: 記事は現在進行中の実際の患者増加ではなく、エルニーニョに関連する気候条件下での将来的なリスク増加予測である。具体的な患者数、入院数、死亡数が報告されていないため、重症度や公衆衛生への深刻な影響は未確認。IDI（インドネシア小児科医学会）からの公式警告があり、予防措置の推奨が示されている。風土病としてのデング熱であるため『異常・予想外』ではないが、気候変動に起因する地理的リスク拡大という点は注目の価値あり。

article.articleHeadline: Pemprov Lampung kembangkan skrining mandiri TBC guna bantu eliminasi kasus
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lampung Provincial Government develops TB self-screening to help eliminate cases.
article.articleSummary: Lampung Province is advancing a TB self-screening initiative via the Peduli TBC Lampung website, in partnership with the Indonesian Pulmonary Doctors Association (PDPI), to support the national TB elimination target by 2030. The platform includes an admin panel and automated WhatsApp notifications to speed up early detection and case finding in Lampung. In East Lampung Regency, estimated TB cases for 2026 reach 3,226, but new case notifications so far total 418 (about 13%), far below the first-half target of 41.25%. Investigations of contacts and uptake of Tuberculosis Preventive Therapy (TPT) are low: of 3,058 household contacts targeted for TPT, only 26 have received therapy (~1%). Data integration between the Free Health Check program CKG and the SITB TB information system is not optimal, and the East Lampung RAD is under discussion. The government calls for regular multi-stakeholder coordination meetings and activation of Desa Siaga TBC for education, screening, contact investigation, and treatment support.

triage.headline_ja: ランプン州政府がTB自己スクリーニングを開発し、症例排除を支援
triage.triage_reason: 結核の制御プログラム進展に関する行政ニュースであり、新規の異常な感染症クラスターや緊急事態ではない。IHR基準およびWPRO基準を満たさず、国際的拡大のリスクも認められない。
triage.notes: 本記事はインドネシア・ランプン州における結核対策強化の行政的な取組みについてのニュースであり、感染症危機シグナルではない。既知の流行地における予防・制御戦略の更新に該当し、新規の公衆衛生上の緊急事態ではない。

article.articleHeadline: Équateur : près de 700 000 enfants ciblés par la campagne de vaccination contre la poliomyélite
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ecuador: nearly 700,000 children targeted by the polio vaccination campaign.
article.articleSummary: Polio vaccination campaign targets 640,825 children aged 0–59 months in Équateur Province, Democratic Republic of the Congo. The three-day drive runs June 18–20, 2026, following a June 17 launch in Mbandaka 3, Wangata health zone, led by the province’s vice-governor Thomas Boyenge Ifaso. The door-to-door strategy will administer four drops of polio vaccine to each child under five across 18 health zones. WHO’s Lado Addoulaye (Mbandaka) emphasizes preventing wild poliovirus circulation as the DR Congo reports 10 poliomyelitis cases in 2026, with 9 in Maniema and 1 in Haut-Lomami. The campaign is organized by the Ministry of Public Health and the Expanded Program on Immunization, with technical and financial support from WHO, UNICEF, Gavi, and Rotary International. The article does not provide laboratory confirmation details or information on imported/exported cases.

triage.headline_ja: 赤道州：ポリオワクチン接種キャンペーンで約70万人の子どもを対象—コンゴ民主共和国
triage.triage_reason: ポリオは国際保健規則（IHR）上の通知義務疾患であり、DRCが2026年に10例（マニエマ州9例、ハウト・ロマミ州1例）を報告している。野生型ポリオウイルス循環阻止の必要性が記事で強調されており、IHR基準（異常性、重症度ポテンシャル、国際拡大リスク）に該当する。
triage.notes: ポリオは撲滅候補疾患で、野生型ウイルスの検出は国際的に重大な懸念。DRCでの複数州での報告は地域的な流行リスクを示唆。WHO、UNICEF、Gavi、ロータリーインターナショナルなど複数の国際機関が対応に関与している点から、国際的な関心と支援の必要性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: СЗО: Во ДР Конго и во Уганда 75 здравствени работници се заразени со ебола
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: In DR Congo and Uganda, 75 health workers have been infected with Ebola.
article.articleSummary: WHO reports 75 health workers infected with Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda, with 17 deaths; it remains unknown whether infections occurred at work or in private life. WHO Bunia representative Marie-Roseline Belizer notes ongoing support to small clinics, including gloves and protective clothing and staff training to prevent transmission. Of 177 clinics surveyed, only four initially had capacity and equipment to protect all personnel. A key challenge is that only about 10% of Ebola infections present with bleeding symptoms, delaying care-seeking and increasing transmission within families and small clinics. Overall, 896 confirmed Ebola cases and 232 deaths have been reported in DR Congo and Uganda as of 2026-06-19.

triage.headline_ja: WHO：コンゴ民主共和国とウガンダで75人の保健労働者がエボラに感染
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラウイルス病は重篤な公衆衛生上の影響を示し、複数国での感染拡大、医療従事者の感染増加は異常である。国際的な拡大リスクと渡航制限のリスクがある。
triage.notes: 記事はコンゴ民主共和国とウガンダの両国での感染を報告しているが、対象国リストではDRCのみが該当する。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため除外。896確定症例、232死亡との報告あり。医療従事者感染とその経路不明確性、貧弱な感染予防対策が示されており、管理可能性の低さが懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: الصحّةُ العالميّةُ: 896 إصابة مؤكّدة بالإيبولا و232 وفاة في الكونجو الديمقراطية
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization: 896 confirmed Ebola cases and 232 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 June 2026, the World Health Organization reports 896 confirmed Ebola virus disease cases and 232 deaths in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, roughly one month after the outbreak was declared. The WHO confirms ongoing response efforts, including deployment of more than 115 experts and the shipment of 110 metric tons of emergency supplies to support field operations, with 78 patients having recovered. Despite these measures, the response faces significant challenges, notably access to high-risk districts, tracing of contacts, and the need for additional funding to curb transmission and contain the outbreak. The figures reflect a concerted international effort in the first month of the response.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機構：コンゴ民主共和国でのエボラ確認患者896人、死亡者232人
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つ全て該当。エボラウイルス病は公衆衛生上の深刻な影響、国際的拡大リスク、渡航・貿易制限のリスク、および異常性を有する。WPROスクリーニング基準も全て該当し、フルRRA実施必須。
triage.notes: エボラウイルス病の急性流行。WHO公式報告で896確認患者、232死亡（約26.0%のケースファタリティレート）。発症から約1ヶ月の段階で、既に115名以上の専門家派遣、110メートルトンの緊急物資供給など国際的対応が進行中。しかし高リスク地域へのアクセス困難、接触者追跡の課題、資金不足など重大な制限要因が存在。国際支援継続が不可欠。

article.articleHeadline: 17 медици загинаха от ебола, СЗО предупреждава за недостиг на защитни средства | Новини.бг
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 17 healthcare workers died of Ebola, WHO warns of a shortage of protective equipment | News.bg
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has infected at least 75 health workers, with 17 fatalities, according to the WHO quoted by Reuters. The virus likely circulated quietly for months before the epidemic was officially declared on May 15, exposing dozens of doctors, nurses, and orderlies to risk while treating patients unaware of infection. WHO Emergency Director Mari Roseline Belizer notes the health system is paying a heavy price, with about 11 health workers per 10,000 people—one of the world’s worst workforce shortages. China and Uganda are sending medical teams to assist, and WHO is providing psychological support to staff fearful after colleagues’ deaths. A dwindling supply of protective equipment—gloves, masks, and protective clothing—further increases risk to frontline personnel.

triage.headline_ja: 17名の医療従事者がエボラで死亡、WHOが防護装備の不足を警告
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つ全て該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）。WPRO基準も5つ全て該当。ハイリスク病原体によるアウトブレイク。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはDRCでのエボラ流行を主題としており、ChinaとUgandaは支援国として言及されているため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとした。医療従事者への深刻な影響、防護装備不足、国際的支援体制の存在が確認される。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : les femmes plus vulnérables à la contagion par Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: Women more vulnerable to Ebola infection
article.articleSummary: In Bunia, Democratic Republic of the Congo, women are identified as the most vulnerable to the Ebola epidemic due to traditional caregiving roles in families and communities. Women frequently attend to the sick at their bedsides, bathe, feed, and launder clothing, increasing exposure to the virus, according to Furaha Elisabeth, director of the Karibuni Wa Maman Gynecology and Obstetrics Clinic. ONU Femmes reiterated on May 22 that women have been overrepresented among Ebola victims for fifty years and warned the current outbreak could reproduce the same pattern. If a woman is infected, she may transmit the virus to those around her, especially children and other dependents she cares for. Government data reported 282 confirmed Ebola cases in the DRC, with 264 in Ituri province, as published Sunday.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国（DRC）：エボラ感染に対する女性の脆弱性
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルス病の確認症例が発生しており、IHR基準で公衆衛生への深刻な影響（死亡・重症化）と国際的拡大リスクに該当。WPRO基準でも重症度と流行しやすさが認識され、シグナル識別基準を満たす。
triage.notes: イトゥリ州ブニアでのエボラ発生。確認症例282件（イトゥリ省264件）が報告されている。女性がケアラー役として特に脆弱であることが強調されており、社会的関心も高い。WHOへの通知対象イベント。

article.articleHeadline: Refugee camp deaths raise fears of new disease outbreak in the Congo
article.articleSummary: In Ituri province, Democratic Republic of Congo, at least 10 people (8 children, 2 adults) died at the Kigonze refugee site within 48 hours, triggering urgent medical investigation amid the ongoing Ebola outbreak. Victims did not show haemorrhaging; the children had fevers and anaemia, while living conditions at the site are extremely difficult. Ituri’s long-standing ethnic conflict—led by groups such as CODECO and CRP—has left aid scarce since 2021, hindering disease response. The Ebola outbreak has expanded sharply, with cases up nearly 40% in the past week to about 900 and around 200 confirmed deaths from the viral haemorrhagic fever. The Bundibugyo species is believed to have circulated for months before the May 15 outbreak declaration. Experts warn the crisis could become the largest Ebola outbreak since 1976 and may take up to a year to control, with public health work disrupted by conflict and mistrust.

triage.headline_ja: 難民キャンプの死亡がコンゴでの新しい疾病の発生の懸念を引き起こす
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準において公衆衛生への深刻な影響（症例数増加と死亡報告）、異常性（48時間以内の複数死亡、原因不明の症例）、国際的拡大リスク（Ebola拡大）の3基準に該当し、さらにWPRO基準でも重症度（死亡事例）、流行しやすさ（難民キャンプでのヒト-ヒト感染リスク）、管理可能性（紛争地域での医療対応困難）に該当するため、フルRRA実施が必要である。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーに基づき、イベントはDRC（Ituri州）で実際に発生しており、Bluedot APIが正確に特定している。既知のEbola発生の拡大局面に新たな死亡事例（原因不明の可能性）が加わり、難民キャンプという高リスク環境での感染拡大懸念が存在する。紛争による医療対応困難が深刻なリスク要因である。

article.articleHeadline: СЗО: 75 медици са заразени с ебола в ДР Конго, 17 са починали
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: 75 healthcare workers infected with Ebola in DR Congo, 17 have died.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 June 2026, 75 healthcare workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo have been infected with Ebola, with 17 deaths, according to Reuters citing the World Health Organization. The outbreak has spread covertly for months before local authorities officially declared it on 15 May, leaving many medical staff exposed without knowledge of the danger. The situation is worsened by a critical shortage of essential protective equipment, including masks and gloves. WHO emergency response officials warn that the health system is paying a high price due to insufficient healthcare workers in the DRC. The country already ranks among the lowest globally for health-worker density, with about 11 workers per 10,000 people, highlighting systemic capacity challenges during outbreaks.

triage.headline_ja: WHO: エボラ出血熱でコンゴ民主共和国の医療従事者75人が感染、17人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラウイルス病は致死性が高く公衆衛生への深刻な影響、医療従事者の大量感染は異常、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限のリスクを示唆。
triage.notes: エボラウイルス病の大規模集団発生。医療従事者への感染と死亡の報告は感染管理の深刻な失敗を示唆。数ヶ月間の隠れた拡散後の公式宣言、個人保護装備の不足、低い医療従事者密度など、システムレベルの脆弱性が存在。WHOによる警告が示す通り国際的支援の必要性が高い。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : le chef de l'OMS est en Ituri, épicentre de l'épidémie d'Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: The head of the WHO is in Ituri, epicenter of the Ebola outbreak.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) centers in Ituri province, with Bunia as its capital and entry point; the airport is closed to commercial flights. The DRC declared a new Ebola outbreak on May 15, and the WHO has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. The Ebola virus, a highly hemorrhagic and contagious pathogen, has spread to three Congolese provinces and to neighboring Uganda, where two new cases were confirmed on Friday, bringing Uganda’s total confirmed cases to nine. In DRC, Africa CDC reports over 1,000 suspected cases and 246 deaths, with Ituri accounting for the majority of confirmed cases. Access to services is limited in rural areas, and armed groups impede response activities. WHO Director-General Tedros is in Bunia to engage communities and support the response.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国：WHOの長官がエボラ流行の中心地イトゥリにいる
triage.triage_reason: エボラウイルスの発生であり、IHR基準4項目全てに該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常/予想外、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限）。WHO公衆衛生上の国際的懸念事象（PHEIC）宣言済み。
triage.notes: エボラ感染症は最重要監視対象。DRCでの発生（1,000件超の疑い例、246死亡）、ウガンダへの拡大（9例確認）、アクセス困難な農村地域、武装勢力による対応阻害が懸念。WHO事務局長の現地訪問は国際的な対応の重要性を反映。PHEIC宣言によりフルRRA必須。

article.articleHeadline: RDCongo.- La OMS confirma 75 trabajadores contagiados de ébola, 17...
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DR Congo - WHO confirms 75 workers infected with Ebola, 17....
article.articleSummary: 75 health-care workers infected with Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo since the current outbreak began, with 17 deaths (case-fatality ~20.46%). The outbreak has approached 900 cases in DRC and over 230 deaths confirmed; declared May 15, with the WHO declaring a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on May 17. Protective measures include PPE distribution and psychological support for health workers; a Chinese medical team has arrived in Bunia, Ituri Province to assist, while Uganda plans to deploy a team at the Arua border. In Uganda, 19 cases have been reported: 14 imported from DRC and 5 locally acquired. The DRC, which ended the Kasai Ebola outbreak in December 2025, is experienced in Ebola response, but the current outbreak remains a major public health challenge.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国 - WHOがエボラ感染の医療従事者75人を確認、17人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常/予想外、国際的拡大のリスク、渡航・貿易制限のリスク）。WHO公衆衛生緊急事態（PHEIC）宣言済みで、複数国への拡大（ウガンダでの症例確認）が認められている。
triage.notes: 発生地域にUgandaが含まれているが、記事サマリーではウガンダは14件が輸入症例（DRCからの輸入）、5件が二次感染であり、主要な発生地はDRCである。DRCは対象国リストに含まれるため verified_locations に含める。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため除外。WHO PHEIC宣言済み（2026年5月17日）で、国際的な対応レベルが最高度である。

article.articleHeadline: La epidemia de ébola se propaga rápidamente en la RDC, advierte la OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Ebola outbreak is spreading rapidly in the DRC, WHO warns.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is accelerating as of 19 June 2026. Since declaring on May 15, the Bundibugyo ebolavirus strain has caused 896 laboratory-confirmed cases and 232 deaths, with 21 new cases in the last 24 hours. It mainly affects Ituri province in the northeast, which accounts for over 90% of cases, and has spread to North Kivu and South Kivu. The World Health Organization reports rapid transmission but improving response: more than 500 treatment beds (up from zero), about 400 alerts daily, and over 2,000 tests per day. Contact tracing covers 75% of contacts; reaching 95% is considered necessary to control the outbreak. Safe burial practices are being emphasized to reduce transmission. In neighboring Uganda, 19 cases, 2 deaths, 10 recoveries; no new cases in 12 days.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ流行がコンゴ民主共和国で急速に拡大、WHOが警告
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つ全て該当。Bundibugyo ebolavirus株による急速な拡大、896の確認症例と232人の死亡、隣国ウガンダへの国際拡大により、明らかにシグナルとしてピックアップが必要。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでウガンダの事例（19例、2死亡）も言及されているが、ウガンダはBluedot APIの対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations から除外。DRCは対象国に含まれており、このイベントの主要な発生地。Ituri州で全体の90%以上の症例が報告され、急速な伝播状況が指摘されている。接触者追跡率75%という段階的な改善があるが、制御には95%の達成が必要とのこと。

article.articleHeadline: La OMS confirma 75 trabajadores contagiados de ébola, 17 de ellos...
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO confirms 75 workers infected with Ebola, 17 of them....
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has infected 75 health workers since the current outbreak began, with 17 deaths (≈20.5% fatality among the infected). WHO confirmed the figures in a Geneva briefing, noting ongoing support for healthcare workers through psychological help and PPE distributed in Ebola centers and other facilities. Ground zero is Bunia, Ituri Province, where a Chinese medical team has arrived to assist; Uganda will deploy a team at the Arua border. Of 19 Ugandan cases, 14 were imported from the DRC and 5 were locally infected in Uganda. The outbreak has nearly 900 cases in the DRC and more than 230 confirmed deaths. It was declared May 15, and the WHO followed two days later with a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. DR Congo had ended its Kasai Ebola outbreak in December 2025.

triage.headline_ja: WHO、エボラウイルス感染の75人の労働者を確認、うち17人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当し、複数国での流行確認、高い致命率（20.5%）、WHO PHEICの宣言があるため、フルRRA対象。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーはウガンダの輸入症例（19例、うち14例がDRC由来）についても言及しているが、ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれていないため、verified_locationsはDRCのみとする。エボラ出血熱はWPRO基準5項目すべてに該当し、WHO PHEIC宣言済み、国際的支援（中国医療チーム、ウガンダ国境への配置など）が既に実施されている。

article.articleHeadline: إيبولا يحصد أكثر من 200 ضحية في الكونغو الديمقراطية وسط صعوبات أمنية تعرقل احتواء الوباء
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola claims more than 200 lives in the Democratic Republic of the Congo amid security challenges hindering outbreak containment.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 June 2026, Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has claimed more than 200 lives. The outbreak is concentrated in eastern regions where armed conflict and widespread population displacement are ongoing, conditions that hinder containment. Health authorities and international partners continue containment efforts, yet UN officials warn that the deteriorating security situation in eastern DR Congo constitutes an additional obstacle to controlling transmission and increases the risk of further spread. The report underscores how violence and insecurity in the country’s east challenge outbreak response and access to affected communities, reinforcing the critical need for safer conditions to advance containment.

triage.headline_ja: エボラウイルスがコンゴ民主共和国で200人以上の死者を出す、セキュリティ上の困難が感染症対策を妨害
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準において4項目すべてに該当。エボラは極めて高い死亡率を有し、200人以上の死者発生は深刻な公衆衛生影響。武装紛争下での東部での流行は異常・予想外。東部地域の難民流出による国際拡大リスク高い。感染症対策困難により国際支援が必要。WPROスクリーニング基準でも全5項目該当。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーは東部コンゴ民主共和国での紛争・難民流出下のエボラ流行を明記。200人以上の死者、保健システムへのアクセス困難、国際パートナーによる対応継続中。UN警告として東部の安全保障悪化による感染拡大リスク指摘。全基準に該当し、PICKUP相当。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola: Health workers battle virus and stigma
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Congo and Uganda remains severe as health workers face infection risk and community stigma. Dr. Jemima Mugisa, 40, works at a government- and ALIMA-run Ebola treatment center. Early in May, her children feared her return from the hospital, and she worried about infecting her family, though conditions have since improved. There is no official tally of healthcare workers infected or died, but at the outbreak’s start several healthcare workers were infected; four recovered and at least one died. The Congo-Uganda outbreak has claimed more than 200 lives in its first month and is the worst known to date, with up to 35,000 suspected contacts. As of June 19, 2026, Africa CDC reports 894 confirmed cases, and the current outbreak is about three times larger than Uganda’s 2000 outbreak, which had 281 active cases.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ: 医療労働者がウイルスと社会的偏見に立ち向かう
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の重大な集団発生が確認され、IHR基準の4項目すべてに該当する。200人以上の死亡、894確認症例、35,000人の接触者追跡中という深刻な公衆衛生影響と、国際的な拡大リスクが明確である。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーに基づき、Congo（DRC）とUgandaの両国が言及されているが、ウガンダはGeoNames IDが対象国リストに含まれていないため、DRCのみをverified_locationsに含める。本件はWHO通知対象の確定事案であり、即座にフルRRA（Rapid Risk Assessment）実施が必須。

article.articleHeadline: СЗО алармира: 75 медици от ДР Конго са заразени с ебола, досега 17 са починали
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO warns: 75 medical workers in DR Congo have been infected with Ebola; 17 have died so far.
article.articleSummary: 75 health workers in the Democratic Republic of Congo have been infected with Ebola, with 17 deaths reported to date, as the outbreak unfolds. The epidemic likely circulated for months before Africa’s first official declaration on May 15, and stocks of basic PPE (gloves, masks) are running low. DR Congo remains among the lowest in health workers per capita worldwide (about 11 per 10,000 people). China and Uganda are sending medical teams to assist, while WHO is providing psychological support to frontline staff. Ebola, a highly contagious viral disease, spreads mainly through contact with infected secretions; the virus can also persist in the skin and, after apparent recovery, remain in the male reproductive system for 7–8 weeks, posing a risk of sexual transmission. A vaccine has been available since 2019; the natural animal reservoir remains unknown. In Africa, Ebola-Zaire, Ebola-Sudan, and Ebola-Tai have caused outbreaks; Reston virus, identified in monkeys in the US/Italy, is not known to cause disease in humans.

triage.headline_ja: WHO警告：コンゴ民主共和国の医療従事者75人がエボラ感染、うち17人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の大規模集団感染で、医療従事者75人感染・17人死亡という重大な公衆衛生影響を示し、IHR基準4項目すべてに該当する。国際支援（中国・ウガンダからの医療チーム派遣）が既に行われており、ワクチン利用可能にもかかわらず流行制御が困難な状況。
triage.notes: 記事は2026年6月19日付けという未来日時を持つが、実質的には現在の進行中のエボラ流行を報道している。発生地域にはアフリカ全体、米国、イタリア、中国、ウガンダが含まれているが、サマリーの主題はDRC内の感染で、中国・ウガンダは支援国として言及されているのみ。したがって verified_locations はDRCのみ。医療従事者への集中的な感染は医療施設内での二次感染を示唆し、感染制御に深刻な課題がある。

article.articleHeadline: La Union cites bird flu risk in disposal of over 20,000 seized eggs
article.articleSummary: Over 20,000 eggs were seized from a dealer at the San Fernando City public market in Pangasinan after a shipment of 30,240 eggs was found misdeclared (declared 9,000). A total of 21,240 eggs were confiscated and disposed at the San Fernando City landfill as unsafe for consumption, presumed to originate from areas designated red zones for avian influenza (bird flu). Authorities warned consumption could pose a serious threat to human health. Some residents questioned how unsafe status was determined since all eggs traveled in a single delivery van. The dealer, Carmelo Aguinaldo, 70, of Tayug, Pangasinan, received a violation for misdeclaration under Provincial Ordinance No. 4187-2023; the report did not indicate avian influenza-origin. La Union Governor Mario Ortega pledged continued strict veterinary border-control protocols to protect public health and consumer safety.

triage.headline_ja: ラ・ユニオン州、2万羽以上の押収卵処分における鳥インフルエンザリスクを指摘
triage.triage_reason: パンガシナン州での押収卵処分に関連する潜在的な鳥インフルエンザ曝露リスクが報告されているが、実際の感染症症例報告ではなく、感染症の流行証拠が限定的であるため。情報不足のため続報監視が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は鳥インフルエンザの潜在的リスク（赤ゾーン地域からの卵の可能性）を報告しているが、確認された人間感染症例や動物感染の実例がない。パンガシナン州の地方当局が厳格な獣医検査境界管理を実施中。信頼できる感染症情報の確認が必要。

article.articleHeadline: الصحة العالمية: إصابة 75 من الكوادر الطبية بفيروس إيبولا في الكونغو
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: World Health Organization: 75 healthcare workers infected with Ebola virus in Congo
article.articleSummary: An Ebola virus disease outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has sickened 75 healthcare workers and killed 17 since the current outbreak began, according to the World Health Organization. WHO’s Emergency Director, speaking via video from eastern Congo, called the toll on the health system a high price, noting a critical shortage of health workers in the country. The agency is providing psychological support to staff fearful of caring for patients after learning colleagues were infected, while China and Uganda are sending medical teams to assist. Authorities say the virus began spreading months before first official cases were reported on May 15, underscoring gaps in infection control amid severe shortages of personal protective equipment such as gloves and masks. Congo already suffers a stark health workforce gap, with about 11 health workers per 10,000 people.

triage.headline_ja: 世界保健機関：コンゴでエボラウイルスに75人の医療従事者が感染
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目全て該当。エボラ出血熱の流行は公衆衛生上深刻で、医療従事者への感染拡大、死亡例発生、複数国への国際支援要請が認められ、国際的な拡大リスクが高い。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーで明示されているDRCでのエボラ流行が主題。中国とウガンダが医療支援チームを派遣しており、Chinaは対象国に含まれるため verified_locations に追加。ウガンダは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。医療従事者への感染（75名）と死亡例（17名）により重症度が高く、感染制御不足と医療資源の極度の不足により管理可能性が低い。

article.articleHeadline: مديرة الاستخبارات الوطنية الأمريكية المستقيلة تولسي جابارد: واشنطن دعمت تجارب صينية مرتبطة بانتشار كورونا
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Former U.S. Director of National Intelligence Tulsi Gabbard: Washington backed Chinese experiments linked to the spread of the coronavirus.
article.articleSummary: Declassified US documents, released amid debate, allege links between US-funded research and the Wuhan Institute of Virology in Wuhan, Hubei, China, involving Anthony Fauci and the White House COVID-19 task force. Former DNI Tulsi Gabbard says the materials include internal emails, whistleblower claims, and intelligence reports on the pandemic’s origins. They purportedly show Fauci supervised funding of coronavirus research on bat coronaviruses at the Wuhan Institute of Virology and remained in contact with intelligence officials during key reviews. Gabbard emphasizes that the documents expose government funding for laboratories—over 120 labs in more than 30 countries—hidden from public view with claims they did not exist. Fauci has denied misleading Congress, calling the accusations “ridiculous” during a June 2024 testimony. COVID-19 emerged in late 2019 in Wuhan; WHO declared a global pandemic in March 2020, causing millions of deaths worldwide.

triage.headline_ja: 元米国防情報局長トゥルシ・ギャバード：ワシントンはコロナウイルス拡大と関連する中国の実験を支援した
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は過去のCOVID-19パンデミック（2019-2020年）の起源に関する政治的・歴史的論争であり、現在進行中の新規感染症イベント（公衆衛生上の脅威）ではない。既知の過去イベントの政治的議論に該当する。
triage.notes: 記事はCOVID-19パンデミック発生後の政治的・外交的論争（米国から中国の研究機関への過去の資金提供に関する主張）であり、現在の感染症脅威シグナルではない。シグナルトリアージの対象外（歴史的論争・陰謀説の報道）。

article.articleHeadline: DSÖ: KDC'deki Ebola salgınında durum ciddiyetini koruyor
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: The Ebola outbreak in the DRC remains serious.
article.articleSummary: As of June 19, 2026, the Ebola outbreak declared in May in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) remains serious, affecting both the DRC and Uganda and caused by Bundibugyo Ebola virus. WHO reports at least 75 health workers have become infected, 17 of whom have died, with virus circulation likely months before official detection and PPE shortages complicating response. The WHO risk assessment lists the national Ebola risk in the DRC as “very high,” with new areas and cross-border movement increasing risk to neighboring countries. Case counts are rising quickly, but testing capacity limitations, security challenges, and regional resistance hinder accurate assessment, leading aid groups to warn that current figures may understate the outbreak’s impact. International efforts emphasize contact tracing, expanding laboratory capacity, and community engagement to control spread. No approved vaccine or specific treatment exists for Bundibugyo Ebola virus.

triage.headline_ja: WHO: KDC（コンゴ民主共和国）のエボラ流行は深刻性を保持している
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目全て該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、予想外の流行、国際的拡大リスク、渡航・貿易制限リスク）。Bundibugyo Ebola virusによる確認された流行で、医療従事者の感染・死亡、国境を越えたウガンダへの波及が報告されており、フルRRA対象。
triage.notes: DRCでの確認流行。ウガンダへの波及も記事に言及されているが、DRCが主発生地で、ウガンダは影響国。対象国リストにUgandaが含まれていないため verified_locations はDRCのみ。Bundibugyo Ebola virusは致死性が高く、医療従事者17名の死亡、テスト能力の制限、セキュリティの課題により対応が複雑化している。国家レベルのリスク評価「very high」、新規地域への拡大と国境を越えた移動が懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: Македонец се заразил со зика вирус на Малдиви
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: A Macedonian has contracted the Zika virus in the Maldives.
article.articleSummary: First registered Zika virus infection in Macedonia confirmed by the Institute of Public Health (IHP). A Macedonian citizen who recently stayed in the Maldives from May 20–28, 2026, contracted Zika likely through a mosquito bite. Symptoms included fever, muscle and joint pains, mild elevated temperature, followed by a body rash several days later. Laboratory confirmation by IHP's Virology Department; patient not hospitalized and receiving home treatment; currently in good health. Although an imported case, rising travel to tropical destinations such as Maldives, Thailand, Indonesia, Brazil, and Caribbean countries raises the possibility of additional cases among travelers. Health authorities assess population risk as low at present, but advise mosquito bite prevention and adherence to travel health guidance for travelers to tropical regions. Ongoing monitoring for new cases, especially among returning travelers, is recommended.

triage.headline_ja: マケドニア人がモルディブでジカウイルスに感染
triage.triage_reason: マケドニアでの初確認感染例（輸入症例）であり異常性がある。しかし現在の人口リスク評価は低く、対象国（マケドニアは対象外）での発生ではなく、患者が海外で感染した輸入症例であるため、直ちにPICKUPの閾値には達しない。ただしジカウイルスの可能性と国際的な警戒対象として経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーの詳細分析：マケドニア市民がモルディブで感染した輸入症例であり、対象国リスト内ではマレーシア（モルディブ）でのみ該当。サマリーではタイ、インドネシア、ブラジルが言及されているが、これらは「旅行先の可能性」として列挙されているのみで、実際の発生地ではない。IHR基準は2つ以上該当（異常性＋国際的拡大リスク）し、WPROスクリーニング基準も2つ該当するが、患者が重症でなく現在の人口リスクが低いと評価されているため、PICKUP判定ではなくWATCH判定とした。ジカウイルスは典型的に国際的拡大リスクと流行しやすさがあるため、継続的な監視が推奨される。

article.articleHeadline: RDC : le ministère des affaires sociales mobilisé pour la prise en charge des enfants rendus vulnérables par Ebola
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: DRC: The Ministry of Social Affairs Mobilized to Provide Care for Children Rendered Vulnerable by Ebola.
article.articleSummary: DRC's Ebola response in Ituri Province centers on protecting and caring for children affected by the outbreak. Minister Eve Bazaiba announced a government-led, UNICEF- and Korea-supported program to host 0–17-year-olds whose parents died of Ebola or are critically hospitalized, with temporary care facilities near response centers. When a case is confirmed or suspected in a family, uninfected children are directed to these centers, which function like nurseries or specialized orphanages and provide multidisciplinary oversight by nannies, doctors, nurses, and psychologists. The goal is to safeguard both health and psychosocial wellbeing amid trauma. The minister also highlighted support for displaced people and refugees and reinforced preventive messaging at reception sites. The initiative follows prior actions in Isiro, Haut-Uele. The briefing was co-hosted by Minister of Communications Patrick Muyaya and Health Minister Roger Kamba.

triage.headline_ja: DRC: エボラにより脆弱化した子どもたちへのケア提供に社会問題省が動員
triage.triage_reason: DRCでのエボラ流行における子どもへのケア体制強化が報じられている。IHR基準で深刻な公衆衛生影響（Yes）と国際的関心（Yes）が該当し、WPROスクリーニング基準では異常性（Yes）・重症度（Yes）・流行しやすさ（Yes）・管理可能性支援の必要性（Yes）が複数該当。政府高レベル（保健大臣・社会問題省大臣）による公式発表および国際機関（UNICEF、韓国）の支援参画により、社会的・政治的関心が高い。
triage.notes: 記事はDRCのイトゥリ州（Ituri Province）およびハウト・ウエレ州（Haut-Uele）でのエボラ流行対応について報じている。イシロ（Isiro）での先行実施事例も言及されており、複数地域での継続的な流行が示唆される。DRC政府がUNICEFおよび韓国と連携した公式プログラムを発表していることから、DRC国内での流行が確認・継続中と判断される。

article.articleHeadline: WHO:Ebola ta kashe jami'an lafiya 17 a Dimukuradiyyar Kwango
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: Ebola has killed 17 health workers in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has killed 17 health workers and infected 75 since it began on May 15, 2026. WHO officials reported the figures as of June 19, 2026, highlighting a persistent shortage of health workers in the DRC that undermines outbreak response. Marie Roseline Belizairene, WHO's Africa regional director, stressed the gap amid ongoing transmission and fatigue among frontline staff. In response, China and Uganda have begun sending teams to bolster the Ebola response in the DRC. The country already suffers one of the world's worst health-workforce gaps, with roughly 11 health workers serving 10,000 people, a ratio that complicates surveillance, case management, and community engagement.

triage.headline_ja: WHO:エボラがコンゴ民主共和国クワンゴ州の保健労働者17人を殺害
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラ出血熱の確認事例であり、死亡者・感染者が報告され、国際的支援（中国・ウガンダ）が既に投入されている深刻な公衆衛生事象。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーの主題はコンゴ民主共和国でのエボラアウトブレークであり、中国とウガンダは支援を送っている国として記述されている。DRCは対象国リストに含まれるが、UgandaとChinaはBluedot APIの発生地域に含まれているにもかかわらず、サマリーでは支援提供国として述べられているため、verified_locationsから除外。2026年5月15日開始、6月19日時点で感染者75名・死亡者17名（全て保健労働者）という極めて重大な事象。

article.articleHeadline: Ebola en RDC : la peur du virus entraîne la stigmatisation des soignants
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola in the DRC: Fear of the Virus Leads to the Stigmatization of Healthcare Workers.
article.articleSummary: Outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda has reached unprecedented levels as of 19 June 2026. In Ituri's Rwampara, Dr. Jemima Mugisa, 40, works at an Ebola treatment center established with ALIMA support, directly treating patients under constant risk. Fear initially affected her family; PPE protocols helped restore trust. Frontline health workers remain among the most exposed; several infections have been recorded and at least one death among health workers since the crisis began. Africa CDC reports more than 200 deaths in a month, 894 confirmed cases, and up to 35,000 contacts potentially exposed. The outbreak is described as the largest Ebola surge ever recorded in the region, surpassing Uganda's 2000 outbreak. Medical teams call for vigilance and rapid patient care.

triage.headline_ja: RDCのエボラ：ウイルスへの恐怖が医療従事者の汚名をもたらす
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラ出血熱の大流行で200人以上の死亡、894例の確認症例、35,000人以上の接触者が報告されており、公衆衛生への深刻な影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク、渡航・貿易制限の可能性があり、フルRRA実施が必須。
triage.notes: 発生地域にはRwanda（キガリ州）、Uganda、DRCが記載されているが、記事サマリーの主題はDRC（Ituri州Rwampara）とUgandaでのエボラ流行。対象国リストではDRC（203312）のみが含まれるため、verified_locationsはDRCのみ。UgandaおよびRwandaは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。記事は2026年6月19日の配信であり、現時点での実時間データとしては将来日付であるが、シナリオ演習と判断して処理。Africa CDCによるシチュアショナル・アウェアネスが高く、国際的対応が始まっている状況が明記されている。

article.articleHeadline: Ébola: Aceleração da transmissão do vírus na RDCongo - OMS
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Ebola: Acceleration of virus transmission in the DRC - WHO.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 June 2026, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is accelerating. WHO reports 896 cases and 232 deaths (case fatality ~26%) across 33 health zones in three provinces; Uganda has 19 confirmed cases, with no new cases in 12 days. WHO deployed 115 specialists and shipped over 110 tons of emergency supplies, yielding 516 beds and capacity for more than 2,000 tests daily. Contact tracing stands at 75% (target 95%), while transmission persists among communities and displaced populations. A Chinese medical team has arrived in Kinshasa. IOM reports over 1 million border checks along RDC and neighboring routes as cross-border surveillance expands. UNHCR warns of rapid spread to displaced communities. Bundibugyo Ebola has no approved vaccine or specific treatment; transmission is via direct contact with bodily fluids; symptoms include fever, vomiting, diarrhea, and internal bleeding. The outbreak began in May and affects eastern DRC and Uganda.

triage.headline_ja: エボラ：コンゴ民主共和国でのウイルス伝播の加速化 - WHO
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目全て該当。エボラ出血熱の急速な拡大、複数国への国際的拡散、高い死亡率（約26%）、国境を越えた流行拡大が確認される。フルRRAへの進行が必須。
triage.notes: Ugandaも発生地域に含まれているが、記事サマリーではUgandaは19確定例で12日間新規患者がなく、主要な流行地はDRCである。DRCのKinshasa市の急速な伝播加速が主題。WHO、IOM、UNHCRが関与し、国際的な対応が展開中。Bundibugyo Ebola（ワクチン未承認株）であることが重要。

article.articleHeadline: СЗО: 75 здравствени работници заразени со ебола во Конго и Уганда, 17 починале
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: WHO: 75 health workers infected with Ebola in Congo and Uganda, 17 have died.
article.articleSummary: During the current Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, the World Health Organization reports 75 health workers infected and 17 deaths. WHO representative in Bunia, Marie-Roseline Belizaire, says it remains undetermined whether infections occurred at work or in private settings. Protection efforts include gloves, protective clothing, and additional training, extending to the smallest facilities. Of 177 clinics surveyed, only four had adequate equipment and capacity to fully protect workers. About 10% of infections present with typical Ebola symptoms such as bleeding, causing many to seek care for malaria first, delaying treatment and fueling spread within households and clinics. To date, 896 Ebola cases and 232 deaths have been reported across the DRC and Uganda.

triage.headline_ja: WHO: コンゴとウガンダでエボラに感染した保健労働者75人、17人が死亡
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当（公衆衛生への深刻な影響、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）。エボラ出血熱の流行で死亡者が多く、複数国での発生が確認されており、フルRRA対象。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーでDRCとウガンダの両国でのエボラ流行が言及されているが、対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみのため verified_locations はDRCのみ。ウガンダは対象国に含まれていない。保健労働者への感染が特に懸念される点。多くの症例が典型的症状を呈さず、マラリア治療を求めるため診断遅延が生じている。

article.articleHeadline: Bundibugyo virus outbreak: when a concerning pathogen meets a humanitarian emergency - Nature Reviews Microbiology
article.articleSummary: Bundibugyo virus (BDBV) outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and neighbors intensified after Kinshasa confirmed BDBV in Ituri Province. At that point, 246 suspected cases and 80 suspected deaths were recorded; confirmed cases later surfaced across several DRC provinces and in Kampala, Uganda. The WHO declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern on 17 May; Africa CDC followed on 18 May with a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security, naming ten other high‑risk countries. By 31 May, 336 confirmed cases and 49 confirmed deaths, plus 220 suspected cases and 236 suspected deaths in the DRC; true infections are likely higher, with Imperial College modelling suggesting more than 900. Most cases remain in Ituri, but infections have been confirmed hundreds of kilometres away in North and South Kivu. Active conflict and funding gaps hinder access; a 28 May WHO appeal for a ceasefire aims to support containment. Lab confirmation delays—negative Ebola tests in Bunia, specimens sent to Kinshasa—hampered response. Vaccines/therapies are in trials but months away; outbreak could extend into 2027 with cross-border risk.

triage.headline_ja: Bundibugyo virus（バンディブギョウイルス）の流行：懸念すべき病原体が人道的危機と出会う場合—Nature Reviews Microbiology
triage.triage_reason: Bundibugyo virusの大規模流行がDRCおよびウガンダで発生し、WHO・Africa CDCが公式な国際的・大陸的公衆衛生上の緊急事態を宣言。IHR基準4項目全てに該当し、国際的拡大とヒト-ヒト感染の急速な進展が確認されている。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーではBundibugyo virus（BDBV）の流行がDRCとウガンダで発生していると記載されているが、対象国リストに含まれるのはDRCのみ（ウガンダは対象国に非該当）。WHO、Africa CDCともに緊急事態宣言済み。感染者数は336確認例・49確認死亡、疑い例を含めると900超の可能性。Ituri、North Kivu、South Kivu州で確認。ワクチン・治療薬は数ヶ月先、2027年までの流行長期化を懸念。紛争地域での対応困難が強調されている。

article.articleHeadline: Congo Ebola outbreak 'remains serious' with nearly 900 cases, WHO says
article.articleSummary: Congo Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo remains serious and continues to evolve one month after it was declared, with 896 confirmed cases and 232 deaths reported across 33 health zones in three provinces. Uganda, a neighboring country, has not reported any new Ebola infections in 12 days. So far, 78 people have recovered. WHO has deployed more than 115 experts and delivered over 110 metric tons of emergency supplies to support response operations. Despite progress, operational needs are rising as access constraints in high-risk areas, gaps in contact tracing, and ongoing community deaths persist; some transmission chains may occur outside the reach of response activities, particularly in displacement-affected communities where needs exceed resources. “We know what works to stop Ebola transmission,” and the agency urges applying those measures at speed and scale to bring the outbreak under control.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱流行は「深刻なままで」、ほぼ900症例、WHOが述べる
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4項目すべてに該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常/予想外、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限リスク）。エボラ出血熱の確認症例896、死亡232、複数州での継続拡大は明確なシグナル。
triage.notes: ウガンダは発生地域に含まれているが、記事サマリーでは「過去12日間の新規感染報告なし」と述べられており、DRCが主要な流行地。ウガンダはtarget countriesリストに含まれないため、verified_locationsはDRCのみ。エボラ出血熱は最優先度疾患であり、確認症例数、死亡数、地理的拡大、継続的な伝播、コミュニティでの死亡事例により、フルRRA実施が必須。

article.articleHeadline: Reuters узнало о заражении Эболой более 70 медиков в ДР Конго
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Reuters has learned of more than 70 healthcare workers infected with Ebola in DR Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo continues to strain health systems, with 75 healthcare workers infected since the current outbreak and 17 of them dead. Infections occurred largely before the outbreak was officially announced, and PPE shortages—gloves and masks—persist. The country’s health workforce density is very low (about 11 per 10,000 people). EU support of €493 million is pledged for frontline outbreak response and regional humanitarian aid in the Great Lakes region and Uganda. As of June 9, WHO confirmed 550 Ebola cases in DRC with 101 deaths, with the Ituri province remaining the epicenter, accounting for 487 cases (94% of total). These figures highlight the ongoing outbreak and the critical burden on Ituri’s health facilities.

triage.headline_ja: ロイターが報道：コンゴ民主共和国でエボラウイルスに感染した医療従事者が70人以上
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準で4つすべてに該当し、WPROスクリーニング基準でも5つすべてに該当。エボラウイルス病は重篤で、DRCで進行中の大規模流行であり、国際的な支援が必要とされている。
triage.notes: Bluedot APIはオーストラリアをも発生地域として付与しているが、記事サマリーではDRCとウガンダ地域でのエボラ流行が主題であり、オーストラリアは検証対象外。DRCは対象国リストに含まれるため verified_locations に含める。550件の確認済みケース、101件の死亡、医療従事者75名が感染（17名死亡）、PPE不足、EU支援€493百万が言及されており、重大で進行中の公衆衛生上の危機を示している。

article.articleHeadline: Число погибших от лихорадки Эбола в Конго превысило 230 человек
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The number of deaths from Ebola virus disease in Congo has surpassed 230.
article.articleSummary: Death toll from Ebola virus disease in the Democratic Republic of Congo has risen to 232, with 896 confirmed cases to date. The latest report, published June 18, records 21 new cases and 6 deaths in the previous 24 hours. Health authorities say weekly increases in confirmed cases demonstrate ongoing person-to-person transmission and that the outbreak remains uncontrolled. Officials warn of a serious risk of further spread and say the outbreak could rapidly reach new areas within the country unless timely public health measures are implemented. The figures reflect laboratory-confirmed cases. The report underscores the urgent need for timely public health actions to halt transmission.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴのエボラ出血熱による死亡者数が230人を超過
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当。エボラ出血熱は重篤な感染症で、232人の死亡、896人の確認患者が報告されており、人-人感染による持続的な流行があり、国内の新地域への拡大リスクが高い。
triage.notes: エボラ出血熱の活動的な流行。過去24時間で6人の死亡を含む21人の新規確認患者が報告されており、制御不能な状態が続いている。記事サマリーは明確にコンゴ民主共和国での発生を述べており、DRCは対象国リストに含まれている。緊急のフルリスク評価（RRA）実施が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Число жертв вспышки Эболы в ДР Конго превысило 200 человек
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The death toll from the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo has surpassed 200 people.
article.articleSummary: An Ebola outbreak declared in May in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has killed over 200 people. Since May 15, confirmed cases reached 875 with 202 deaths (case fatality rate 23%). The outbreak is concentrated in Ituri (about 95% of cases) and has spread to North Kivu and South Kivu; Uganda reports 19 cases and 2 deaths. Africa CDC has expanded testing and digital epidemiological surveillance to speed case detection. International donors and partners pledged about $910 million to support the response in DRC and Uganda, including $80 million from African Union member states within a $100 million fund. The DRC allocated $50 million for its national response, while Uganda provided $5 million in initial funding. Africa CDC Director Jean Kaseya warned that uncontrolled spread could be worse than the 2014–2016 West Africa Ebola epidemic. Congolese Health Minister Samuel Roger Kamba visited Bunia to assess progress, difficulties, and new localization strategies.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴ民主共和国のエボラ出血熱流行による死亡者数が200人を超過
triage.triage_reason: エボラ出血熱の大規模流行で200人以上の死亡、国際的な資金援助動員、複数国への拡大（DRC、ウガンダ、隣接州への広がり）が報告されており、IHR基準4項目すべてとWPRO基準5項目すべてに該当。政府・国際的関心も高く、即座にフルRRA対象。
triage.notes: Uganda（226074）は発生地域に含まれているが、記事サマリーでは「ウガンダが19症例と2死亡を報告」と述在例報告に限定されており、主たる流行発生地はDRC（Ituri、North Kivu、South Kivu）。対象国リストではDRCのみが該当するため、verified_locationsはDRCのみ。エボラ出血熱は極めて高い致死率と国際的な拡大リスクを持つため、シグナルピックアップは確実。Africa CDCによる警告、国際的な資金援助（9.1億ドル）、複数省庁の対応が記載されており、社会的・政治的関心は最高レベル。

article.articleHeadline: 17 медици загинаха от ебола в Конго: Китай и Уганда изпращат помощ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 17 medics died of Ebola in Congo: China and Uganda are sending aid.
article.articleSummary: As of 19 June 2026, 17 medics have died from Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo as the outbreak intensifies. Official data show 75 health workers infected, with 896 total cases and 232 deaths; Oxfam cautions that true figures are likely higher. The outbreak was officially confirmed in mid-May but is believed to have begun weeks earlier, risking many clinicians before recognition. The DRC has one of the world's lowest health-worker ratios, about 11 per 10,000 people. WHO emergencies director Marie-Roseline Belizer stressed the burden on frontline staff and the need for mental health support. China has dispatched a medical team, and Uganda is sending specialists after 19 cases and two deaths. Africa CDC reports a 38% weekly rise in infections. The outbreak is caused by the Bundibugyo Ebola strain, for which no approved vaccine or specific treatment exists, making this the heaviest such outbreak to date.

triage.headline_ja: コンゴでエボラにより17人の医療従事者が死亡：中国とウガンダが支援を派遣
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4つすべてに該当し、スクリーニング基準も5つすべてに該当。エボラ出血熱は公衆衛生上の重大な脅威であり、国際的な支援体制が既に機能している。
triage.notes: エボラ出血熱（Bundibugyo株）による大規模流行。医療従事者の死亡率が高く、DRCの医療システムが脆弱。中国とウガンダからの国際支援が確認されており、WHOも対応を強化。週間感染率38%増という急速な拡大が懸念される。記事ではウガンダでも19症例と2死亡が報告されているが、サマリーの主題はDRCのアウトブレークであるため、DRCのみを verified_locations に含める。

article.articleHeadline: Uma epidemia sem vacina, sob ameaça de grupos armados: Ebola volta a se espalhar na República Democrática do Congo
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: An epidemic without a vaccine, under threat from armed groups: Ebola spreads again in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
article.articleSummary: Ebola spreads in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, centered in Ituri's Bunia. Early reports: 246 suspected cases and 80 deaths; Uganda later confirmed 19 cases and 2 deaths, calling one an imported Congolese case and closing the border. WHO declared a public health emergency of international concern; Africa CDC warns about risk across ten African countries. The Bundibugyo strain has no vaccine or specific treatment; vaccines currently protect only against the Zaire strain, so containment relies on isolating patients and tracing contacts. Bunia airport closure interrupts aid logistics. Within weeks, nearly 1,140 suspected cases and 246 deaths were reported; a week after the outbreak was declared, 204 deaths among 867 suspected. May 5 alert described a lethal unknown disease in Mongbwalu; local labs lacked Bundibugyo reagents. MSF warns of slow response; US tightened visas for risk-area travelers; several countries imposed entry restrictions; Tedros visited Kinshasa and Bunia.

triage.headline_ja: ワクチンなしの流行、武装勢力の脅威下で：エボラが再びコンゴ民主共和国で拡大
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準4項目すべてに該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク、渡航制限の実施）。WPRO基準も全5項目該当。WHO国際保健上の緊急事態宣言済み。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーではウガンダの症例確認と国境閉鎖が記述されているが、主たる発生地はDRCのイトゥリ地域（ブニア）であり、ウガンダは輸入症例として言及されているため、verified_locationsにはDRCのみを含める。Bundibugyo株による流行で、ワクチン不在が重大な懸念要因。WHO国際保健上の緊急事態宣言、複数国の入国制限実施、アフリカCDCによる広域警告など、社会的・政治的関心も極めて高い。

article.articleHeadline: Rollout of 5,000 Near Point-of-Care TB Test Systems in 13 Countries Begins With $50M in Funding
article.articleSummary: TB diagnostics rollout begins with about $50 million to deploy 5,000 MiniDock Ultra instruments and 3 million TB tests across 13 countries (Bangladesh, Benin, Cameroon, Ethiopia, Indonesia, Kenya, Nigeria, Peru, the Philippines, South Africa, Uganda, Vietnam, Zambia). Tests use RNase HII-assisted amplification (RHAM) isothermal chemistry, enabling rapid TB diagnosis from tongue swabs at roughly half the cost of decentralized molecular testing.
